body.purpose: Standard interface copy and form content.

label.purpose: Control labels and concise row labels.

metadata.purpose: Timestamps, counts, paths, refs, and supporting status details.

shadows.name: small
shadows.purpose: Sparing broad diffuse low-opacity depth for complete cards and secondary synchronization facts.

shadows.name: medium
shadows.purpose: Broad diffuse low-opacity depth for floating menus, hover cards, and tooltips.

motion.name: reduced
motion.purpose: Reduced-motion duration; essential status text remains present.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Primary action for a decisive local workbench operation.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 36px; padding: 0 12px; border: 0; border-radius: var(--gs-semantic-radius-control); background: var(--gs-component-button-primary-background); color: var(--gs-component-button-primary-foreground); font: 500 13px/1.35 Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif; transition: background-color 180ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--gs-component-button-primary-hover); } .ds-btn-primary:active { background: var(--gs-component-button-primary-pressed); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--gs-component-button-focus-ring); outline-offset: 1px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Neutral secondary action distinguished by solid inset tone, without a default outline.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 36px; padding: 0 12px; border: 0; border-radius: var(--gs-semantic-radius-control); background: var(--gs-component-button-secondary-background); color: var(--gs-component-button-secondary-foreground); font: 500 13px/1.35 Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif; transition: background-color 180ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1); } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: var(--gs-component-button-secondary-hover); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--gs-component-button-focus-ring); outline-offset: 1px; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Low-emphasis action that reveals an inset hover surface.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 36px; padding: 0 12px; border: 0; border-radius: var(--gs-semantic-radius-control); background: transparent; color: var(--gs-semantic-text-secondary); font: 500 13px/1.35 Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif; transition: background-color 180ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1), color 180ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1); } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: var(--gs-semantic-surface-inset); color: var(--gs-semantic-text-primary); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--gs-component-button-focus-ring); outline-offset: 1px; }

components.name: Accent Button
components.description: Pastel microaccent for a selected or navigational context, not a saturated primary block.
components.css: .ds-btn-accent { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 36px; padding: 0 12px; border: 0; border-radius: var(--gs-semantic-radius-control); background: var(--gs-semantic-selection-background); color: var(--gs-semantic-selection-text); font: 500 13px/1.35 Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif; transition: background-color 180ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1); } .ds-btn-accent:hover { background: var(--gs-semantic-feedback-info-surface); } .ds-btn-accent:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--gs-component-button-focus-ring); outline-offset: 1px; }

components.name: Danger Button
components.description: Destructive action with a labelled error surface and text.
components.css: .ds-btn-danger { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 36px; padding: 0 12px; border: 0; border-radius: var(--gs-semantic-radius-control); background: var(--gs-semantic-feedback-error-surface); color: var(--gs-semantic-feedback-error-text); font: 500 13px/1.35 Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif; transition: background-color 180ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1); } .ds-btn-danger:hover { background: var(--gs-semantic-feedback-error-surface); } .ds-btn-danger:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--gs-component-button-focus-ring); outline-offset: 1px; }

components.name: Field
components.description: Text field for branch names, paths, and other repository values.
components.css: .ds-field { box-sizing: border-box; width: 100%; height: 36px; padding: 8px 12px; border: 1px solid var(--gs-component-field-border); border-radius: var(--gs-semantic-radius-control); background: var(--gs-component-field-background); color: var(--gs-component-field-text); font: 400 13px/1.35 Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif; } .ds-field::placeholder { color: var(--gs-component-field-placeholder); } .ds-field:hover { border-color: var(--gs-component-field-border); } .ds-field:focus { border-color: var(--gs-component-field-focus-border); outline: 0; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--gs-component-field-focus-ring); } .ds-field:disabled { cursor: not-allowed; background: var(--gs-component-field-disabled-background); opacity: 0.65; }

components.name: Success Badge
components.description: Text-labelled success status for checks and completed states.
components.css: .ds-badge-success { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; padding: 2px 8px; border: 0; border-radius: var(--gs-semantic-radius-pill); background: var(--gs-component-badge-success-background); color: var(--gs-component-badge-success-text); font: 500 12px/1.4 Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif; } .ds-badge-success:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--gs-component-button-focus-ring); outline-offset: 1px; }

narrative.overview:
Git Stacks is a quiet, precise desktop workbench with a soft rounded card system for navigating branches, stacks, pull requests, changes, history, and stashes. Clean, uncluttered layouts and generous whitespace establish hierarchy through confident typography, spacing, scale, and alignment. A light cool-gray canvas, white cards, and near-black type form the neutral foundation; the dark theme preserves the same hierarchy with corresponding neutral tones. Pastel microaccents support small indicators, progress, selection, and labelled semantic status, never large saturated decorative fills. Borders and dividers are a last resort, and decorative elements are almost absent. Clarity wins over decoration.

Workbench Ink anchors primary actions and readable text. Repository Blue supports links, focus, selection, checked-out state, and meaningful graph edges; independent labelled semantic colors communicate Git states. Large rounded cards group complete existing domain objects. Sparing broad, diffuse, low-opacity shadows and small offsets on secondary cards support spatial hierarchy and interactivity without turning operational lists, diffs, forms, or safety dialogs into decoration. No gradients or glass are introduced.
keyCharacteristics: Cool-gray workspace canvas with white content surfaces and inset grouping surfaces.
Neutral ink primary actions, with pastel microaccents for small meaningful selection, indicators, and labelled status details.
Independent, text-labelled Git states for selection, checked-out state, pull-request lifecycle, checks, review, restacks, and diffs.
Compact information density for branch, pull-request, stash, history, and diff rows.
Local-first, keyboard-accessible, operation-safe behavior with no external font or network dependency.

rules.name: The Meaning Before Color Rule
rules.body: Every selection, checked-out branch, pull-request lifecycle, checks state, review decision, restack requirement, and diff role has an explicit text or icon meaning. Unknown or unavailable GitHub data uses the neutral unknown role and an explicit unavailable label; it is never represented as none, zero, or passing.

rules.name: The Essential Boundary Rule
rules.body: Separate UI groups with spacing and solid tonal surface differences first. Borders are a last resort for separation: surfaces, cards, rows, section headers, and status badges do not receive decorative outlines by default. Inputs, editable controls, keyboard focus, meaningful graph/diff lines, and deliberately connected controls retain a visible boundary where discoverability requires it, using semantic.border.essential or semantic.focus.ring. Keep border tokens meaningful; do not hide every border with a global override. Use sparse diffuse card shadows only where they serve layering or interactivity, never gradients or glass.

rules.name: The Code Is Monospace Rule
rules.body: Use the system monospace stack for code, paths, refs, and OIDs; use the system sans stack for interface copy. No external font is loaded and no font files are copied from chat artifacts.

rules.name: The Purposeful Layering Rule
rules.body: Use diffuse depth sparingly to clarify a real card or floating layer. Secondary cards may use a 4px spatial offset with disciplined internal alignment: the catalog inspection/checkout composition and real synchronization facts demonstrate this. Do not rotate operational Git rows, diffs, forms, or safety dialogs, obscure actions, or imply Git state through shadow. Never introduce sharp or dramatic shadows, glass, or decorative gradients.

rules.name: The Related Spacing Rule
rules.body: Unrelated siblings must not touch. Use 8px between related controls and label/help/error content, 12px between fields and fact groups, and 16–24px between major sections. Shared surface content and card footer actions supply explicit gaps; catalog compositions separate identity/action rows, conversation drafts, and captured-result feedback. Dense metadata may use 4px, but not zero-gap action clusters. Deliberately connected button groups, segments, tables, code cells, and graph joins retain their connected geometry.

dos: Do use neutral Workbench Ink for primary actions and text, with pastel microaccents and contrast-correct labelled semantic colors for small meaningful states.
Do keep selection, checked-out state, pull-request lifecycle, checks, review, restacks, and diff additions/deletions/hunks independent and explicitly labelled.
Do use the 4px spacing rhythm, 36/44px controls, 44/56px rows, and the user-retained rounded 12/16/24px geometry with supported 999px pills.
Do use semantic.border.essential for essential boundaries, semantic.focus.ring for keyboard focus, and text/icon descriptions alongside every Git status.
Do define primitive, semantic, and component tokens in packages/ui/src/tokens/tokens.json; treat tokens.css as generated output, never a second manually maintained palette.
Do keep the renderer local-first, preserve the sandbox/preload/IPC/CSP boundary, and retain busy-state text when reduced motion removes animation.

Do share production controls, typography and foundations through @git-stacks/ui; catalog specimens demonstrate this implementation rather than defining a second visual policy. Keep larger content typography distinct from compact application roles.
Do keep essential boundaries at ≥3:1 against their adjacent surface in both themes; the dark essential-border primitive is #657185 so shared editable controls retain this distinction.
Do keep normal text and placeholders at ≥4.5:1 and large text at ≥3:1; use weights 400/500/600, left-aligned readable copy, and the compact 14px/1.5 body role.
Do use simple Lucide icons consistently, add labels for ambiguous actions, place feedback near its field, and use progressive disclosure rather than repeated guidance or metadata.
Do prioritize spacing and solid tonal contrast over borders for grouping; preserve essential editing, focus, and meaningful graphic boundaries instead of applying blanket border suppression.
donts: Don't globally replace --accent with ink; selection, links, checked-out state, and stack graphics remain Repository Blue, while merged pull requests remain violet.
Don't use color alone for status, lifecycle, review, checks, unknown/unavailable data, or diff meaning.
Don't use decorative semantic.border.decorative dividers as a substitute for essential control boundaries or meaningful graphics.
Don't add external font loading, font files from chat artifacts, a second manually maintained palette, CRM runtime behavior, or new Git/IPC/navigation semantics.
Don't add arbitrary shape overrides, excessive pills, decorative gradients, glass, sharp dramatic shadows, or gratuitous nested boxes. Preserve generous rounded cards and circular icon controls.
Don't use ornamental scale, bounce, parallax, or excessive motion; purposeful state transitions use 100–250ms and preserve meaning with reduced motion.
Don't use shadows or card offsets to imply Git state, invent metrics, or obscure operational controls. Purposeful secondary layering must preserve focus, scrolling, and action reachability.
